name: Man Industries (India) Limited
tagline: Strong Q1 FY27 turnaround and a large order book cannot offset an active SEBI order for financial misrepresentation — EXCLUDE
business_overview: Man Industries manufactures LSAW, HSAW, and ERW steel pipes for oil & gas and water infrastructure, with export-focused capacity in Anjar (Gujarat) and domestic-focused capacity in Pithampur (MP), plus a newly acquired Saudi Arabia facility (National Pipes Company, ~Rs 1,000 Cr, Q4 FY26).
fundamentals_table: Revenue +38% YoY, PAT +118% YoY, EBITDA margin 14.6% vs 10.4%
Rs 3,600 Cr + Rs 24,000 Cr bid pipeline
fundamentals_narrative: Q1 FY27 shows a genuinely strong operating turnaround (revenue +38%, PAT more than doubling, EBITDA margin expanding ~420bps) backed by a large order book and bid pipeline including the new Saudi Arabia capacity. In isolation, this would be a strong methodology-fix candidate. However, this is overridden by a confirmed regulatory finding described below.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass given the EXCLUDE-tier finding below.
sentiment_summary: Long-running thread (since 2022) with a persistent undercurrent of governance concern: a SEBI forensic-audit letter in Feb 2022 (fund-diversion concerns related to the promoter family's Merino real-estate dealings), a qualified auditor opinion over a Rs 70 Cr related-party transaction to 'Marina Shelter' (2024), and NFRA imposing a 5-year ban on the company's statutory auditor (Nov 2023) following a SEBI referral. This culminated in a confirmed SEBI order.
community_signal: rupaniamit (2025-09-30, 22 loves) posted a detailed history of the promoter family split (JM Mansukhani's sons RC and JC) and the origins of the governance concerns, directly following the SEBI order — a widely-engaged, well-researched community post rather than a conviction call.

trusted_signals.note: "Have increased portfolio weights behind bets where I think that growth rates can be faster + valuations r not expensive" — listed alongside Time Technoplast and Entero Healthcare (post #1874). This mention predates full weighting of the confirmed SEBI order's implications and is overridden by the red flag below.

bse_notes: SEBI issued a confirmed order (Sept 2025) finding that Man Industries (India) Ltd. and three of its directors misrepresented financial statements — non-consolidation of subsidiary accounts, undisclosed related-party transactions, and fund rotation — between FY2015-16 and FY2020-21. The company and three executives were barred from the securities market for 2 years and fined Rs 25 lakh each. The company obtained a stay from the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) in Oct 2025 after paying 50% of the penalty — meaning the matter is stayed/under appeal, not resolved or cleared.
bull_case: Q1 FY27 shows genuinely strong operating momentum (PAT +118% YoY) with a large, diversified order book including new Saudi Arabia capacity
A ranvir (trusted) mention exists on growth-rate/valuation grounds
bear_case: SEBI has issued a confirmed order finding financial misrepresentation by the company and three directors, covering a 5-year period (FY2015-16 to FY2020-21) — this is precisely the kind of active regulatory action this project's EXCLUDE tier exists to catch
The SAT stay (after paying 50% of the penalty) means the matter is under appeal, not cleared — it remains an active, unresolved regulatory action as of this scan
NFRA separately banned the company's statutory auditor for 5 years following a SEBI referral related to the same underlying issues
A qualified auditor opinion on a separate Rs 70 Cr related-party transaction (2024) suggests governance concerns are not confined to the pre-2021 period covered by the SEBI order
verdict_headline: EXCLUDE — an active SEBI order for financial misrepresentation overrides genuinely strong recent operating results and the trusted mention
verdict_reasoning: Per this project's ground rules, a confirmed active SEBI/regulatory action always overrides a trusted mention and strong recent fundamentals — this is exactly that case
The SEBI order (Sept 2025) is confirmed, covers financial misrepresentation across a 5-year period, and remains under appeal (SAT stay) rather than resolved, so it counts as 'active' as of this scan

The Q1 FY27 operating turnaround is real but does not change the governance assessment — a company willing to misrepresent consolidated financials for 5 years is not a name this project can respond to on operating metrics alone
Not flagged for 30-day revisit given the EXCLUDE tier — this would need the SAT appeal to fully resolve, not a routine 30-day check, before being worth reconsidering
red_flag_reason: SEBI order (Sept 2025) found Man Industries and three directors misrepresented financial statements FY2015-16 through FY2020-21 (non-consolidation of subsidiary accounts, undisclosed related-party transactions, fund rotation), barring them from the securities market for 2 years and fining Rs 25 lakh each. The company obtained a SAT stay in Oct 2025 after paying 50% of the penalty — an active, unresolved appeal, not a cleared matter.
